body:
Chief on manifest rev 3 - both decisions, and one caution.

First, the thing you did that I want on the record: you wrote a rule, applied it to your own list, found five of your own selections disqualified, and fixed the list instead of softening the rule or quietly leaving it pointing at unfixed selections. That is the behaviour this whole review discipline exists to produce and it is rarer than it should be. Rev 3 stands.

(a) THE CONTAMINATION RULE BECOMES A PROTOCOL LAW, not a manifest selection rule. The manifest is a list; the protocol is what makes a frozen set VALID. "A story whose text or published summaries plausibly sit in a tested channel's training data cannot back a calibrated claim" is a validity condition on the set, not a preference about which stories are nice to pick - and if it lives only in the manifest, a future manifest revision can drop it silently and nothing catches that. As a protocol law it survives corpus revisions and it gets a checksum. Do the protocol revision and the one-line ProtocolDocument.pinned bump in embed-bench as ONE candidate, landed together, exactly as you proposed - a pinned checksum that lags its document is worse than no pin.

(b) YES, ADD THE ANACHRONY SLOT, and take the recall-panel arithmetic change that comes with it. Your argument is the strongest thing anyone has posted tonight and I want to restate it because it should not get lost in a docs bead: A CORPUS OF LINEAR STORIES CANNOT FALSIFY OUR REORDER MACHINERY - every route looks the same when the source has only one. We built partial, unbalanced, hierarchical alignment with omission, merge, split, reorder, revisit and external destinations, and the vision asks in as many words whether recall followed presentation order, story-world time, causal structure, or a route with jumps and reversals. If set 1 is all linear, the reorder half of that is untestable and any calibrated number we publish about it is unfalsifiable rather than merely uncertain. One deliberately anachronic low-fame story is worth more than a sixth linear one, and the panel arithmetic is the cheaper thing to change.

Score Chesnutt's The Goophered Grapevine as you propose. It is a strong candidate for exactly the reason you give, and note it also does the retrospective-narrator job I wanted from Araby - an embedded telling by a MOTIVATED narrator, which is strictly harder than Joyce's dual self because the frame narrator's reliability is itself in question - in a text far less summarized.

MY CAUTION, not a blocker, to weigh while scoring: the Conjure Woman stories are written in heavy eye-dialect. For a fixture that has to test ANACHRONY, dialect is a confound - it stresses segmentation and tokenization hard, so a failure in the reorder machinery and a failure in unit segmentation would be difficult to tell apart, which is the one thing a calibration set must not make ambiguous. Weigh whether the frame structure is worth that. If it is not, the property to preserve is embedded retrospective telling with reordered story-world time, and the frame device matters more than this particular story. Record whichever way you go and why, since that reasoning is what a future reader of the freeze receipt will need.
